# URLs

Parsing a URL into its parts and reading them back.

<h2 id="host-kind"><code>HostKind</code></h2>

```rux
pub enum HostKind: uint8 {
    None = 0,
    Domain = 1,
    Ipv4 = 2,
    Ipv6 = 3
}
```

What a URL's host is. `Copy`.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Url/Src/Url.rux#L17)

**Cases**

| Name     | Value | Description                                                 |
| -------- | ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `None`   | `0`   | The URL has no authority, so no host.                       |
| `Domain` | `1`   | A registered name, such as `example.com`, or an empty host. |
| `Ipv4`   | `2`   | A dotted-decimal IPv4 address.                              |
| `Ipv6`   | `3`   | An IPv6 address, written between brackets in the URL.       |

<h2 id="url"><code>Url</code></h2>

```rux
pub struct Url {
    // private fields
}
```

An absolute URL in normalized form.
Read it with [`Parse`](/docs/api/url/url#parse) and resolve references against it with [`Resolve`](/docs/api/url/url#resolve). Every component is a view of the URL's own
text, still percent-encoded; [`Decode`](/docs/api/url/query#decode) turns one into text. Copying a URL copies its text.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Url/Src/Url.rux#L32)

**Associated functions**

<h3 id="parse"><code>Parse</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Parse(
    allocator: Allocator,
    text: char8[..]
) -> Url ! UrlError
```

Reads `text` as an absolute URL and puts it in normalized form.
Spaces and control characters around the text are ignored. A character a component cannot hold as itself,
such as a space or a non-ASCII byte, is percent-encoded; a host is not, and refuses one.

| Name        | Type        | Description                    |
| ----------- | ----------- | ------------------------------ |
| `allocator` | `Allocator` | what the URL's text is kept in |
| `text`      | `char8[..]` | the URL                        |

**Returns**: the URL, or fails with what is wrong with it; a relative reference fails with `MissingScheme`

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Url/Src/Url.rux#L218)

**Methods**

<h3 id="resolve"><code>Resolve</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Resolve(
    self: &Url,
    reference: char8[..]
) -> Url ! UrlError
```

Resolves `reference` against this URL, as a browser resolves a link on a page, following section 5 of
RFC 3986. An absolute reference stands on its own; `//host/path`, `/path`, `path`, `?query` and `#fragment`
replace what they name and keep the rest of this URL.

| Name        | Type        | Description                             |
| ----------- | ----------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `reference` | `char8[..]` | an absolute URL or a relative reference |

**Returns**: the resolved URL, kept with this URL's allocator

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Url/Src/Url.rux#L229)

<h3 id="set-path"><code>SetPath</code></h3>

```rux

    self: &var Url,
    path: char8[..]

```

Replaces the path. A relative path is made absolute when the URL has an authority.

| ------ | ----------- | ------------------------------------ |

**Returns**: nothing, or fails when the path cannot be normalized
